statements.physics: Physics is the science concerned with describing the interactions of energy, matter, space, and time, and it is especially interested in what fundamental mechanisms underlie every phenomenon. A surprisingly small and unified set of physical laws explains what we observe.

new.name: Quantum mechanics
new.statement: Quantum mechanics is the study of objects smaller than can be seen with a microscope. Together with relativity it makes up modern physics, and it is needed wherever the objects studied are that small.

new.name: SI units
new.statement: SI units, also known as the metric system, are the international system of units that scientists in most countries have agreed to use, named for the French Système International. This text uses them almost exclusively.

new.name: English units
new.statement: English units, also known as the customary or imperial system, are the units historically used in nations once ruled by the British Empire and still widely used in the United States, such as feet, gallons, and pounds.

new.name: Second (s)
new.statement: The second is the SI unit of time. It is defined as the time required for 9,192,631,770 vibrations of the cesium atom.

new.name: Meter (m)
new.statement: The meter is the SI unit of length. It is defined as the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second.

new.name: Kilogram (kg)
new.statement: The kilogram is the SI unit of mass. It was once defined as the mass of a platinum-iridium cylinder kept near Paris, and since 2019 it is defined in terms of the second, the meter, and Planck's constant.

new.name: Length
new.statement: Length is one of the fundamental physical quantities, the distance between two points. Its SI unit is the meter.

new.name: Area
new.statement: Area is the size of a surface, found for a rectangle as its length times its width. Its SI unit is the square meter.

new.name: Volume
new.statement: Volume is the space an object occupies, found for a box as its length times its width times its height. Its SI unit is the cubic meter.

new.name: Approximation
new.statement: An approximation is an estimated value based on prior experience and reasoning.
